reason: The draft is a RENDERED_TEACHER_DRAFT covering unit-1-adviser-peer-demonstration with intent EXPLAIN. Two substantive defects require rejection. DEFECT 1 — Teaching case / assessment case contamination in the EXAMPLE material (mat-example-weak-improved-worse) and the rendered transcript (mat-transcript-adviser-demo): The teaching demonstration uses the fictional teaching cases Stonebrook Tools / Harbor Workshop / DEMO-A-204 / EUR 86.40 / 9 May, which is correct. However, the improved_prompt in the teaching EXAMPLE ends with the standalone sentence 'Keep the tone calm and respectful.' The approved assessment (unit-1-item-1 improved_prompt stimulus) ends its body with 'Keep the email under 150 words.' These are two different detrimental-change illustrations. The teaching draft correctly uses the tone-sentence variant for the EXPLAIN demonstration, and the assessment uses the 150-word variant. The requirement T01 prohibits quoting or solving the assessment removed-length task, and the command requirement R02-F04 specifies that the teaching demonstration must end with 'Keep the tone calm and respectful' as its only tone/style guidance. On this point the teaching draft is compliant. However, the approved_review_notes record an unresolved finding that 'the card EXAMPLE illustration uses [sample text]' — this is a preserved source gap from the historical approval and must not be claimed as repaired. The rendered EXPLANATION material (mat-explanation-prompt-structure) states under EXAMPLE: 'Importantly, a discussion of examples without actually providing one does not enact this move; the sample text must be present in the prompt itself.' This is correct teaching content. But the EXAMPLE section of the explanation does not itself supply an enacted example (no sample text is provided in the explanation body); it only discusses the concept. This is consistent with the approved finding that the card EXAMPLE illustration uses [sample text] as a placeholder — the draft does not repair this and does not claim to repair it, which is correct preservation. DEFECT 2 — shared_materials field is empty in the rendered unit item: The rendered unit-1-item-1 in the draft.units array contains 'shared_materials': [] while material_keys lists all four materials. The command requires that all four materials be referenced in the EXPLAIN item and that every asset the instruction promises be supplied. The rendered item instruction references all four material_keys but shared_materials is empty. The host rendering note states that host rendering establishes structure, not completeness of reasoning or source support, and that shared_materials is a rendered field. However, the rendered output explicitly shows shared_materials as an empty array alongside the populated material_keys, creating an internal inconsistency in the rendered draft that cannot be resolved by host rendering alone — the materials are listed in material_keys but not in shared_materials, meaning the rendered structure does not confirm the materials are actually attached to the item for delivery. This is a structural incompleteness in the rendered output. DEFECT 3 — The approved_review_notes preserve the finding that 'transcript line 21 hints at enacted/mentioned classifications.' The rendered transcript (mat-transcript-adviser-demo) line 13 in the adviser speech (turn 13 in the numbered sequence) contains the sentence: 'So to summarise what we have observed tonight: a bare instruction with no primary content produces a generic output.' This is in the adviser closing speech (turn 13 / paragraph 13 of the transcript content). The approved finding about transcript line 21 hinting at enacted/mentioned classifications refers to the assessment transcript (annotation_transcript line 21), not the teaching transcript, and is preserved as an unresolved assessment gap — the teaching draft correctly does not reproduce or claim to repair it. On this point the draft is compliant. SUMMARY: The primary rejection ground is the empty shared_materials array in the rendered unit item creating a structural incompleteness, combined with the fact that the content_complete flag cannot be set true when the rendered structure shows materials listed in material_keys but absent from shared_materials. Citation support is adequate across all four materials using exact retained document IDs. Intent is correct (EXPLAIN only, no learner submission or practice task). Source alignment is partially compromised by the structural rendering gap. new_gaps is correctly empty. The approved_review_notes findings are preserved and not claimed as repaired.
